In short, a standout fantasy and supernatural anime accompanied by a killer soundtrack, a VERY intricate plot and lore line, and some 10 out of 10 animation. As a standalone, even if you dont think about the other fate series adaptations, it holds its own as an independent enjoyable watch for fans of action. In a seemingly ordinary world, there is a huge war amongst mage masters to see who will claim what the stories lay out to be the “Holy Grail”. Each master is accompanied by a “servant” that has a special archetype and can be summoned practically at their will. The only way theholy Grail can be one is if only one master-servant pair remain remains. This all takes place in a modern city, with civilians (mostly) left out of the war. Masters do not volunteer, they are chosen as part of their “fate”, usually being connected to a line of mages and people in magic. This is where we meet our main character emiya, who does not necessarily wish to participate in the holy girl war, but realizes that he must, as the last winner of the holy Grail war destroyed everything around him.



I have to admit the plot to start off slow, but the different characters and events that are happening slowly get explained as the story goes on. I do wish there were certain things that were slightly explained more like how some servants can command other servants and maybe a little more backstory on certain masters and other characters. But then again, you have to remember that it is part of a long series of animes that are all interconnected so I’ll let it slide. Overall for 12 episodes I think the pacing is good, there is a little room for slice of life moments and not just actions shoved down your throat every minute. The conflicts are very interesting with different characters having different motives to achieve the holy Grail and their unorthodox ways on how they plan to get it. 


Characters are definitely a strong point of this adaptation of the series. Emiya and Tousaka are complete characters with motives, friends, enemies, desires, fears, weaknesses, and strengths. Tousaka was initially indifferent about emiya, saw him as an enemy when she found out, he was a master, almost killed him, then they proceeded to make a truce and save each other’s lives multiple times. Her servant saved emiyas life multiple times as well. And all of the different servants having different archetypes, weapons, and attack styles is dope. At the end, the two main characters true thoughts are known very well and we feel very familiar with them. The only thing I can say that I wish there was more of is just the backstory for certain characters like the priest, shinji/sakura, and the teacher ofc.


Animation is 10/10, classic ufotable. The action sequences are colorful, fast, intriguing, different, 3-D, dynamic. They really did their thing with this one. Sabers “suit up” moments go hard af, the transition is genuinely seamless. Music in the battle scenes is heat too. Very enjoyable series, all of the elements of the story really pull it together to just be a great watch.



8.6/10

I usually don't comment any negative things for any animes, because I truly believe that some shows just aren't for certain people. Different people have different tastes and I get it. However, Tougen Anki is a show that lowered a bar for me that I didn't even know existed. I will admit that the character designs and concept have potential, however, the use of every shounen anime trope in existence..is terrible. School setting, aloof/nonchalant teacher, classmates that are strong but below the main character's strength, main character's rival, main character's father-figure dying, terribly written female characters are just a few of the tropes constantly presentin this show. The Momotaro vs. Oni conflict is bland and boring to put it LIGHTLY. 

But my biggest issue is how BADLY the girls in this show are shown and written. I've watched shows with badly written girls or with alot of fanservice: One piece, Naruto, Soul eater, Fire force, Kill la kill, etc. and I usually am able to skip these parts and just call it a day. However, the proportions of the girls' chests are SO bad, I can't. Every single time a girl is present and shown, its annoying to me. The real question is if the mangaka of this story has ever gone outside and seen an actual woman, or has he been getting sole inspiration from womens' chests from time-skip One Piece...

I usually like to at LEAST watch up to the first season, because I know that sometimes, some animes get better as the story starts to pick up momentum. However, after watching whatever I just watched and pausing this show every 2 minutes to critique it, I am NOT going to be watching season 2 or continuing this series. 

Tbh, I'm a lover, not a fighter. But I PASSIONATELY hate this show. Watch with caution. If you like anime that are equivalent to trashy isekai with alot of harem and fanservice, you will LOVE this show.

From the reviews, I had high hopes for this donghua. However, it became clear this wasn't a show for fans of a real plot or consistent continuity. For example, it appears to take place in a feudal/imperial era but somehow has credit cards? Additionally, the art style is, in my opinion (take it with a grain of salt), bland and, at worst, boring. I thought this would be a fun period piece like Yona of the Dawn, Apothecary Diaries, or The Warrior Princess and the Barbarian King, but no: the characters run flat, there are few redeeming qualities, and the jokes don't land. Like many peoplehere, I was recommended this because I like Yona of the Dawn, Apothecary Diaries, Ancient Magus' Bride, and others, but it pales in comparison. It is better to just skip this one and call it a day.

High school romance anime has a distinct appeal that makes them enjoyable: they’re cute, light-hearted, and for some, nostalgic. But, most franchises fall short from one plot feature that’s heavily overdrawn, which is that pretty much every character is naïve. For some, it’s unbearable to watch. They’re high schoolers, after all, so perhaps I’m discrediting them too much. That’s why it was so refreshing to see this series do things differently. Fundamentally, like any other high school romance anime, yes, this one was about the characters navigating their social and romantic relationships after starting from nothing. But I was surprised by how nuanced their personalities wereand how mature each of them were in resolving their personal tensions within 24 episodes.

Taira stood out to me the most. At first glance, he’s someone who, from past trauma, has an avoidant attachment style. But his own read of his insecurities is so precise, it might trigger viewers who can relate. And the series could’ve easily ended at that since, in reality, many people suffer with this indefinitely. But besides Azuma being a catalyst to his personal growth, he asks himself the right questions - not “Why am I like this?” but “What did I lack before that made me this way, and what can I do now?” The level of self-awareness he has is almost superhuman, and the moments where he overcomes his lack of self-esteem are small, yet very meaningful wins.

That was my interpretation of Taira, and he was just a side character. In fact, I think him and Azuma could be its own separate cour with how in-depth their relationship is. The anime production crew really did something special with this, and watching this has made me look forward to reading Koucha Agasawa’s other works.

Watching this for the first time in 2026 is a bit of a strange experience. Of course, I had heard about this show for a very long time, and as a romance junky, it's a bit of a shame that it took this long for me to get to watching it. Overall, my thoughts are that the show was enjoyable: surprisingly funny, the characters were well-thought out, extremely well-paced for a romance, and the main relationship's dynamic was adorable. But, it hasn't aged well: of course, the animation doesn't look great compared to modern anime (which isn't really a fair comparison, but unfortunately it isone that must be made nonetheless), Usui is straight up problematic (though he is properly considerate about certain things), and the story doesn't do anything particularly revolutionary -- even by 2010 standards. Normally this would be an 8, but the way that Hinata's relationship with Misaki was handled just felt so idiotic that I felt compelled to drop it to a 7. I'm not particularly bothered by competing love interests, nor do I have a problem with the childhood friend trope. But it is just so inconsistent with Misaki's character to not just tell him to drop it. For someone as kind, caring, and outspoken as she is, to not immediately turn him down and establish that this won't lead anywhere for him is both a disservice to him and the plot (especially considering where in the story this whole part started).

Surprisingly the humour in this show was very well written and I found myself laughing a lot more then I thought, the relationships and dynamics are quite interesting and more engaging then I thought it would be too Only thing holding it back is that the animation is very simple but wasn’t unbearable or choppy, I think this would of make a good web series with a lot more episodes (which I do wish it had and I wish they had more episodes to explore character dynamics) but I liked the length of each episode Overall, I would say If you wanna watch a very shortand stupid anime I would definitely recommend watching this

Finally got around and finished this show, and it was amazing ride. It is rather unique, not only because of it's circus themed but also because it is set in 50's era Japan. It is quite refreshing to see an era that is honestly not so active anymore as modern age internet and TV shows pretty much replaced it. Before I start my review a disclaimer: this goes for most obvious critic of this show - that they do not animate circus stunts enough. While this point stands, it is missing the point of this show - and that is focus on the characters dramaand their story. They do focus on them a bit more in the final arc becasue the stunts finally become main focus of the story. So, if you go into this show expecting nothing more but circus life and stunts you will be disappointed. 

The situation is the same as HBO's Rome TV series, whoever watched that knows what I am talking about. I still adore the series despite being literally robbed of epic battles that happened in that era - becasue they were not the the point of the show. It was the political turmoil and events of that age.

Animation and music: great! The animation is standard by today's metric but you can see that they cared about the details. There are no low animation scenes and while they did used still images for most of the performances they did that more to move story forward than to save on the animation, as shown evidently by last arc where they really put effort into them. Music is also very good, no notable tracks to remember but the circus music they used for shows make it unique enough.

Overall - animation and music are done with care, you will not get a feeling that this is budget show.

Characters: to me this is where this show really shines, and true reason to watch it. All the characters that appear in it that are members of Sunflower circus are properly developed and the bonds that exists between them are wonderfully done. Main character Mizuka is lovable little tsundere that makes every scene much better than it should really be. And the rest of the cast is not lagging behind as well. Ouka's strive to recreate famous act, Isuzu and Imari's care for eachother, Akane and Aoi's siblings bond, Svetlana and Shizuku's chemistry and Maria's leadership nature while looking like a toddler are the things that make this show what it is. The other supportive characters are also interesting, especially Nanami with her backstory. So if you go into it expecting various enjoyable characters you will be in for a treat.

Overall - characters and their ups and downs, struggles and success is this shows bread and butter. You will enjoy following their story from 1st to the last episode.

Story: it starts simple enough - Mizuka almost died due to dehydration and was saved by Maria and Ren who are owners of Sunflower circus trope. From that moment Mizuka starts working for them because her dad left a debt and the payment is due. From there the story starts dealing with characters and their backstories, and at some point it becomes very serious but nothing too much dark. Let's just say that Sunflower circus members have to give them their all for the sake of their future, the final arc was so good that the entire journey is worth it. And do not worry too much, despite becoming a bit serious and dark from middle to the end this show is still primarily CGDCT and comedy in nature. 

I will note one more thing that is not mentioned by many in their reviews - this show has some strong yuri vibes. Not among everyone of course, but between those that does it is indeed very strong. Svetlana and Shizuku are unofficial pair, there is no denying that one once you watch the show. But Mizuka and Ouka are not far behind as Ouka is thirsty for Mizuka just like Sahara is for fresh raindrops. It does not help that Mizuka herself is solving problems and "bonding" with people by bathing with them together. She took that right from Amaori Renako book. xD In any case, yeah... the twins and Isuzu and Imari are also there, not to that level as the already mentioned ones but close enough. If you call Sunflower circus the Circus of Useless Lesbians you would not be that far off. xD In any case, if you are also enjoying some yuri than this will only be a bonus for you.

Overall - the story is good and it primarily serves to put the struggles and success of our characters in the light. There is some drama and slight darkness from middle to the end but the show retains it's comedic and CGDCT nature to the very end. 

Overall grade: 10 from me, I quite enjoyed it. Realistically this show is sitting somewhere around 8.5 and 9. The production is great, the characters are amazing, the setting is unique and the story may not be the strongest but it is good enough to bring all the other show strengths into play. Only true fault I will note is what others already said - they could animate more of the circus acrobatics as circus is after all one of the main themes of it. But that is not affecting the entire thing that much and the rest of the show is so good that it more than makes up for it.

Easy recommendation from me. A nice show to enjoy and have a good time overall. I doubt we will ever see sequel as story is pretty much set and done. But if they ever made it I will watch it for sure.

entry.title: Grow Up Show: Himawari no Circus-dan

data.review:
This show does such an incredible job showing the raw struggles of being a mangaka through Rei-sensei’s eyes, while contrasting it with the pure passion of a young, aspiring creator like Ai Yasumi. The dynamic between those two is easily the highlight. Rei goes out of her way at first to keep Ai away from making manga because of her own traumatic past, but eventually gives in after seeing Ai's sheer determination—especially once Ai builds a whole club of friends who share that same drive. I love how Rei plays it cool and cautious on the outside, but is secretly total fangirl status whenever she seesthe club completely locked in on creating. The flashbacks explaining Rei’s past setbacks and burnt-out history really justified why she quit the industry to become a teacher in the first place.

That finale twist hit so well too. Finding out Rei and Ai actually met years ago (with only Rei remembering it) adds so much depth to why Rei was always so overly protective of her. She was genuinely terrified Ai would walk down the exact same self-destructive path if she tried going pro, which is why she pushed so hard for her to just keep it as a hobby. But seeing Rei read Ai’s notebook full of crazy manga ideas and realizing Ai has a totally different mindset and resilience than she did... man, you could just feel that huge weight lifting off her shoulders.

The only thing keeping me from giving this a perfect 10/10 is that it felt like it just lacked that final bit of oomph—that personal spark that completely blows you away. But it's easily a solid 9/10.

Really great show that captures both the harsh reality and the passion for making art.

Negatives: 1. The first few episodes started out pretty slow with everything being confined to the school/classroom setting. 2. It got a bit too heavy on the lore dumps and exposition, overcomplicating things a little too much for its own good. 3. he whole situation with the Dean, the Princess, and the evil/dark Princess version genuinely got super confusing. Between the identity stealing, the body-swapping, and pushing people into mirror dimensions while disguised, it was kind of frustrating to follow at times. Positives: 1. The worldbuilding and lore are still super interesting—especially the concept of ancient civilizations and how they shape the current world. 2. The character dynamics are top-tier. Aliciais an absolute gigachad of a female lead, and her growth since Season 1 is amazing to see. Also love Klen slowly softening up toward humanity.
3. The animation goes completely wild during the fight scenes.

And man... that ending twist to wrap up the arc was diabolical. Klen actually dying and having everyone wait 5 years for his revival was insane, but seeing Alicia’s situation at the end left me completely hooked. Really hoping they handle Alicia’s fate/revival in a well-written way and don't resort to cheap or cliché cop-outs.

Overall a solid continuation despite the mid-season confusion!

entry.title: Clevatess II: Majuu no Ou to Itsuwari no Yuusha Denshou

data.review:
They've started glazing Rimuru on sight. I think what I feared from last season slowly started rearing its head this season, where Rimuru becomes so OP that it feels like there are little to no stakes at all, at least in the first half, and on top of that, it feels like he can do basically anything. The first half of the season was that and it was unbearably boring. I don't mind the slice of life aspect, but so much of it was focused on the dungeon, and it just bored the hell out of me. However, I do think the politics of thealliance was decently entertaining to watch. Finally, when there was some sort of action with Mariabel, it literally was a nothingburger stomp. On top of that, they make it seem like Yuuki was actually controlled and might not be a bad guy, but immediately disprove that, which could have made for a nice plot. He also has an anti-skill move that's sorta revealed but not really important.

One of the biggest problems I've started to see from this show is Raphael. Raphael literally does EVERYTHING in the show for Rimuru, and I genuienely feel like it's killing this show. Every single problem is solved by Raphael, who can do anything from create objects to give Rimuru hyper specific instructions on how to save everything and everyone. It's so boring, and I do miss when Rimuru had to somewhat think for himself in the earlier seasons. He had the great sage, but at least it wasn't a super all knowing entity that solved all his problems.

I will say, the only thing stopping me from giving this season a 6 or lower was the time travel plot with Chloe. Honestly, I wasn't super excited about Granbell Rozzo because I knew somehow Rimuru would one shot him somehow (turns out it was Demon Lord Valentine who did it tho). Even though the Chloe time travel subplot was a bit random and out of nowhere, it was amazing seeing her live the past 2000 years as the hero, and it was also an amazing twist to realize she was the one who sealed Veldora and Hinata took over her body and became Shizu's mentor, who in turn became Hinata's mentor in the future. It's amazing how when the plot isn't focused on Rimuru, the story becomes interesting again, and I think that's a problem when the title of the isekai is about the slime. The author woke up for a bit and actually made an interesting plot, that although rushed, as super interesting. One thing I will say is Rimuru did not give a SHIT about Hinata dying. Literally no fucking emotion at all. Somehow they are making him more unlikeable by the season, and it really confuses me. Of course, in the end Raphael does some bullshit and he revives both Chloe and Hinata. The show treats resurrection as this impossible thing, but Rimuru has done it twice so far, so it's really starting to lose it's impact.

I do think the show wanted you to somewhat sympathize with Granbell, and to a certain extent you do, but I don't think there was enough screentime or backstory for someone to really care.

In all, the first half of this show really showed the future when stakes become less and less big and Rimuru becomes more and more powerful, and while it wasn't awful, it wasn't as good as some of the earlier seasons, but the second half was great at showcasing the importance of some of the other characters in the world, and that some enemies still prove a threat to Rimuru, however Raphael combined with the strength of the characters is starting to make the show more boring to watch and I am truly afraid of the next season.
